title: Lentil and kale bake with parsnip crumble

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain cupboard staple such as tinned tomatoes, stock and breadcrumbs, with no jars, packet mixes or substitutes.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item that Tesco sells at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only an ovenproof casserole and a grater, and the techniques are simple softening, simmering and scattering.

works.reason: 250g red lentils in 700ml stock plus a tin of tomatoes simmers to a thick base, and 500g of grated parsnip with crumbs and oil will crisp in 20 to 25 minutes at 200°C, a sound amount for four.

honest_times.reason: Chopping the onion, garlic and kale and grating the parsnips during the simmer fits roughly 15 active minutes, and the steps add up to the 40 minutes of cook time printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm baked dish suits late March, and 500g of grated parsnip forms the whole crumble topping, the biggest single ingredient, rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear and plain British English that a beginner could follow, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling dinner of lentils, kale, tomatoes and parsnips that a family would happily eat again.
